articles: neon-text-contrast
Check text contrast on animated neon backgrounds
Accessibility
Text may look bright on a game landing page but become unreadable as gradients and moving effects pass behind it.
Evaluate the least favorable background under labels, not only one screenshot. Give text a stable backing panel, maintain adequate size and verify the normal WCAG AA 4.5:1 text contrast target.
For large display text, WCAG permits different contrast treatment than normal text. Do not classify a small glowing status label as large text merely because it is bold.
A translucent panel's contrast can change frame by frame. Test light and dark animation states, different devices and forced-colors presentation.
WCAG,CAN
reduced-motion-playability
Respect reduced motion without hiding essential information
Accessibility
Rapid camera shake, zoom effects and pulsating particles can create discomfort for motion-sensitive players.
Read prefers-reduced-motion, disable decorative oscillation and flashing backgrounds, while keeping hazards visible using static shape and textual cues.
Replace a rapidly pulsing danger ring with a fixed high-contrast dashed outline; this preserves a warning while removing unnecessary movement.
An animation-free mode that conceals attack timing is not playable. Run an entire stage in reduced motion and assess the same win conditions.
WCAG,CAN
polite-win-announcements
Announce meaningful game milestones without a speech flood
Accessibility
Every score change announced through aria-live can produce a nonstop stream of screen-reader interruptions.
Announce stage complete, game over and major status changes using a polite live region. Keep rapidly changing clocks and coordinates readable without automatic speech.
Say 'Stage 8 complete, next stage 9' once; avoid repeating the new point total every time a coin moves across the board.
Replacing the entire live-region element each frame can duplicate announcements. Check output with a screen reader during fast scoring.
LIVE,WCAG
dom-accessible-board
Expose canvas puzzle controls through semantic buttons
Accessibility
Canvas pixels do not automatically describe interactive mirror orientation, coordinates or activation behavior to keyboard users.
Keep the graphical beam on Canvas or SVG but represent clickable grid cells as buttons with row, column and orientation labels. Preserve focused node identity during updates.
A row-three column-five mirror announces whether it is slash or backslash, and Enter changes that state exactly as a touch click does.
A single aria-label on a canvas cannot substitute for dozens of independently operable puzzle cells. Solve a sample level using only keyboard and audio feedback.
WCAG,PTR
upload-errors-readable
Describe image conversion validation failures precisely
Accessibility
A WebP tool that displays only a red border or a generic Error 400 leaves users guessing what needs fixing.
Associate the message with the invalid field and use an accessible live region. Explain allowed types and file-size limits without echoing untrusted HTML.
Use 'Unsupported image: select PNG, JPEG or WebP under 10 MB' rather than relying on a red outline or obscure parser code.
Sanitize any displayed filename and use textContent for untrusted material. Test corrupted files, enormous dimensions and keyboard navigation.
WCAG,INPUT
stable-grid-focus
Keep focus on the same puzzle tile after each move
Accessibility
A rerender that recreates every button may reset browser focus and make repetitive keyboard play exhausting.
Track the selected logical cell and restore focus to its new DOM button after state updates, or update stable elements rather than replacing them.
Rotate cell C4 ten times and use Undo; focus should remain associated with C4 unless an explicit modal or level transition changes the interaction context.
Do not auto-focus an unrelated footer after each move. Test with keyboard, screen reader and zoomed text.
WCAG,LIVE
sound-consent
Require user choice before playing game audio
Accessibility
Sound effects triggered on first load can surprise visitors, conflict with device etiquette and run into autoplay restrictions.
Create or resume an AudioContext only after a user gesture, expose sound-off and volume options, and ensure all essential clues have visual equivalents.
A sound toggle should show its state and immediately prevent further sound, while a muted game remains completely solvable.
Browser suspended audio contexts are normal; do not treat a denied autoplay attempt as evidence a game is broken. Test initial load and tab restoration.
AUDIO,WCAG
zoom-200-percent
Keep settings and instructions accessible at 200 percent zoom
Accessibility
Rigid game overlays can clip the Start button when OS text size grows or the browser zoom is increased.
Use content-driven panel heights, allow vertical scrolling, wrap labels and avoid fixed-width instructions. Keep controls reachable on narrow screens.
At 200% zoom on a 390-pixel viewport, a player should still find Hint, Undo and Restart without horizontal panning.
Disabling user scaling hides the problem instead of fixing it. Test portrait, landscape, large text and browser zoom.
WCAG,IMG
keyboard-trap-audit
Detect hidden keyboard traps in pause overlays
Accessibility
Focus can become trapped on a game canvas or escape behind a modal, preventing users from reaching Cancel or Resume.
Use proper modal semantics, focus management, Escape handling and a visible exit. Respect Tab movement instead of overriding it globally.
Open Pause, Tab through controls, activate Resume, and return to the previously selected puzzle mirror without touching a mouse.
Hidden dialog controls must not remain in the keyboard sequence. Verify native keyboard and assistive technology paths on every screen.
WCAG,PTR
shape-not-only-color
Make safe items and hazards distinguishable without color vision
Accessibility
Danger indicators that rely solely on red versus green fail for players who cannot reliably discriminate that color pair.
Combine color with shape, iconography and concise text, such as a triangle hazard and a circular energy target. Keep differences visible in a grayscale capture.
A grayscale screenshot of a gameplay frame should reveal which symbols are unsafe without requiring the player to memorize a subtle color hue.
Colorblind simulation does not substitute for actual user testing, but it reveals obvious dependence on hue. Also test reduced motion.
WCAG,CAN
